```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library("naboer")
```

Keys identify series. `.by` limits dependence to independent domains. Explicitly
choose whether temporal windows span all series in a domain or stay inside each
series. Ordinary tibbles need explicit metadata; tsibbles supply it.

```{r}
x <- tibble::tibble(
  site = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 12),
  date = rep(as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:11, 2)
)
f <- neighbourhoods(x,
  key = site, index = date, within = "key",
  temporal = temporal_window(time_span(2, "days"))
)
tibble::as_tibble(f, folds = 1:3)
```

Elapsed days are exactly 86,400 seconds. Calendar days follow local civil time
and can span 23 or 25 hours across daylight-saving changes. Calendar months/years
clamp invalid month-end dates. Ambiguous/nonexistent times error unless explicitly
resolved with `time_span()` arguments. Numeric indices are seconds. Tsibble
year-week/month/quarter indices use period-start dates for queries;
`fold_data()` preserves their original class.

An already resolved timestamp retains its exact instant when shifted by zero,
including either occurrence of a repeated daylight-saving clock time. Supplied
POSIXct origins may use another display timezone; calendar arithmetic always
uses the timezone of the data index. Supply timezone-aware timestamps when local
calendar boundaries matter.

Observation-count spans count actual rows and require `within = "key"`. They do
not infer missing observations. Resolve tied times within a counted series first.
Duration windows can include simultaneous observations.

```{r}
blocks <- temporal_folds(x, time_span(4, "days"),
  key = site, index = date,
  within = "domain", origin = as.Date("2024-01-01")
)
tibble::as_tibble(blocks)
```

Windows include both boundaries; adjacent blocks are half-open. Default block
origins are the earliest observation in each selected domain or series.

## Forecasting

An origin defines what was available for fitting. Exclude the gap, then score the
assessment horizon. All later observations remain omitted, including those beyond
the horizon. Origins span all participating series in a domain by default.
This shared cutoff prevents a station's future data from remaining available
while another station is assessed. Use elapsed or calendar spans for dependent
multiple-series forecasting. `within = "key"` is rejected when an independent
domain contains multiple series.

```{r}
forecast <- forecast_folds(x,
  initial = time_span(3, "days"),
  horizon = time_span(2, "days"), gap = time_span(1, "days"),
  key = site, index = date
)
tibble::as_tibble(forecast)
analysis_indices(forecast, 1)
assessment_indices(forecast, 1)
```

Use `window = "sliding"` with `lookback` for finite training history: training
includes times strictly after `origin - lookback` and through the origin.
Generated origins have horizon endpoints no later than the latest observation
in their domain. Individual series may have gaps or end earlier; constructors do
not fill them, and empty generated assessment windows are skipped. Explicit
`origins` require nonempty training and assessment in every participating domain.
Calendar sequences remain anchored to the original date when initial spans and
steps both use months/years or both use days/weeks, preserving leap-day and
month-end boundaries without cumulative clamping drift.

Count-based forecasting supports one series per independent domain. There is no
common observation-count cutoff across asynchronous dependent series. Use a
shared time-based horizon for such data. Setting `.by = site` declares sites
independent: observations from other sites remain available for fitting,
including their later timestamps. Make this choice only when that availability
matches the prediction task. Leave `.by` unset when all stations must share the
same information cutoff.

The fold design controls which observations contribute to fitting and scoring;
it cannot prevent leakage through predictors or preprocessing. Construct
predictors and imputations using only information available at each origin in
explicit-refit workflows. Forecasting may omit a large fraction of the data,
where an NCV approximation need not match full refits accurately. Check the
approximation for the fitted model and omission widths; the reproducible
`benchmarks/approximation.R` study illustrates that comparison.

```{r tsibble, eval=requireNamespace("tsibble", quietly=TRUE)}
series <- tsibble::as_tsibble(x, key = site, index = date)
temporal_folds(series, time_span(4, "days"), within = "key")
```
